lastCommit.message:
OTA-1824 — the helper is called, not quoted

A BOUNDED NATIVE COMPILE REPAIR. One Swift file. No redesign, no feature, no
JS byte, no llama setting, no build-number mechanic, no workflow, no credential.

⚠⚠⚠ ROOT CAUSE, FROM THE XCODE LOG RATHER THAN THE EAS SUMMARY.
The owner dispatched the production HAL build at 5b819d98 (build-ios run 196,
id 34909667987). EAS build 197 (54f56b3e-02a0-46fd-a085-878b76be5cca, Xcode
26.2 / iPhoneOS26.2.sdk, gym 2.231.1) bundled the JavaScript successfully,
reached Xcode, and died in "Run fastlane" at ** ARCHIVE FAILED ** with five
copies of one diagnostic:

    generic parameter 'T' could not be inferred

The failing compile unit names all four of this module's files — the podspec
sets SWIFT_COMPILATION_MODE = wholemodule, so the type checker saw the whole
module and reported everything it found. It found exactly five errors, and all
five are the same line at MemoryFlightRecorder.swift:381, :403, :462, :706
and :740:

    let N = MemoryFlightRecorder.n

⚠⚠ THE MECHANISM. `n` was `static func n<T: BinaryInteger>(_ v: T) -> Int`.
Binding a generic function to a `let` WITHOUT APPLYING IT asks Swift to build a
function VALUE, and a function value must have a concrete type. With no argument
and no contextual type there is nothing from which to fix `T`, so the type
checker refuses. The five aliases were a readability convenience — `N(x)` reads
better than the qualified call inside a long dictionary literal — and they cost
a 25-minute round trip on an EAS macOS worker plus one owner dispatch.

ALL FIVE ERRORS SHARE ONE CAUSE. There is no second defect behind them: whole-
module compilation means the compiler type-checked every file before reporting,
so these five were the complete set.

⚠ THE OTHER LOG LINE IS NOT OURS AND IS NOT AN ERROR. Line 1304 warns
"Pods/Sentry-Sentry: iOS@11.0 deployment version mismatch" — a pre-existing
WARNING on Sentry's own pod, present before this module existed. Untouched.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
THE REPAIR — SMALLEST THAT COMPILES, AND IT MOVES NO MEASUREMENT

The helper becomes a file-scope function and is APPLIED at each of its 63 call
sites, where `T` is inferred from the argument exactly as generics normally
resolve. The five alias lines are deleted.

    -  @inline(__always) private static func n<T: BinaryInteger>(_ v: T) -> Int
    +  @inline(__always) private func tmInt<T: BinaryInteger>(_ v: T) -> Int

    -      let N = MemoryFlightRecorder.n        (x5, deleted)
    -      "footprint": N(vm?.footprint ?? 0),
    +      "footprint": tmInt(vm?.footprint ?? 0),

⚠⚠ NOT ONE MEASUREMENT CHANGED. Every value still passes through
`Int(clamping:)`; the diff is the helper's spelling and nothing else. The
"measurement" lines in the diff are the same expressions with `N(` rewritten to
`tmInt(`. No capacity, cadence, burst rule, signal, threshold or flag moved.

SCOPE AUDIT: 1 file, +93/-77. ZERO .ts/.tsx/.js/.json touched by the repair
itself. `git diff --name-only | grep -E '\.(ts|tsx|js|jsx|json)$'` is empty.

⚠ THE ARCHITECTURE IS UNCHANGED, AND §2 OF THE NEW SUITE PROVES IT RATHER THAN
ASSERTING IT: 512/64 capacities, 1s/5s/100ms cadences, the single shared burst
deadline with its 10 s ceiling, the >=1 s allocator clock, every signal
(phys_footprint, resident_size, resident_size_peak, os_proc_available_memory,
malloc_zone_statistics, thermalState), annotate's no-Mach-on-the-caller rule,
the two-slot CRC32 checkpoint, the bridge's thirteen doors, the exclusion list
and the llama prohibition are each re-asserted here.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
WHY THIS CARRIES 1824 AND NOT A RE-PUBLISH UNDER 1823

The repair is Swift-only and the JS bundle is BYTE-IDENTICAL to OTA-1823's, so
"no new OTA is owed" is the tempting answer. It is the wrong one.

`modules/**` is NOT in ci.yml's publish-ignore list, so this push DOES dispatch
the publisher and a new update group DOES reach both channels. OTA_BUILD_ID is
the value the device DISPLAYS and the one the just-updated toast keys on — so
landing a new bundle under a stamp the device already carries would look exactly
like no update arriving. That is precisely the failure OTA-1482 was written to
stop ("eleven OTAs published and applied while the stamp sat at 1469 and the
owner's phone read fully up to date"), and reproducing it deliberately to save a
number would be indefensible.

The stamp names the PUBLISHED AUTHORITY, not the diff's file extensions.
1824 verified unclaimed before stamping; 1823 demoted to SUPERSEDED, its
published record at 5b819d98 left exactly as it stands.

⚠ 5b819d98 IS NOT REWRITTEN. It remains the published OTA-1823 authority on both
lines. This commit is a NEW exact application authority that supersedes it for
the native build; CI 2161 covers 5b819d98 and is NOT claimed to cover this tree.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
EVIDENCE on the exact committed tree

  new suite ota1824TheHelperIsCalledNotQuoted ............ 16/16
  ota1823 (85) + ota1482 (the stamp law) re-run .......... 106/106
  22/22 check:* gates, read BY EXIT CODE
  check:otastamp — stamp 2026-09-15-1824 matches newest suite ota1824
  source typecheck clean · lint clean
  typecheck:tests at baseline 201 — NOT raised
  FULL TRACKED FAST SURFACE: 1321 suites passed / 1321 total
      14,588 passed · 3 skipped · 0 failed · 498.9 s
      (1320 at OTA-1823 plus this OTA's one new suite — reconciles exactly)
  Heavy CI NOT RUN — a Swift spelling repair does not justify it.

⚠⚠ THE SWIFT STILL CANNOT BE COMPILED HERE. Linux container, no Xcode, no
simulator. The strongest proportional validation available is static: the
repaired construct is the ordinary applied-generic form, every unapplied
reference is gone from code, and the new ratchet fails if one returns. Only the
next EAS build can prove the archive succeeds, and nothing here claims it does.

NEGATIVE CONTROL — NC-196, restored with md5 match and zero residue:
  reintroduce ONE unbound generic reference exactly as build 197 carried it
    -> 1.2 (the general ratchet) and 1.3 (the specific pin) BOTH red,
       the other 14 green.
The ratchet bites the real defect, not a paraphrase of it.

⚠ WHY THE RATCHET IS GENERAL RATHER THAN A STRING PIN. 1.2 walks every generic
function the module declares and requires each mention in CODE to be followed
immediately by `(` or `<`. A pin on the literal text `let N =` would have
matched only the five lines that already burned us; this catches the next one,
under whatever name it is given. Comments are stripped first, so the ⚠ block
that QUOTES the defective line for the next reader cannot trip it — a ratchet
that fires on its own explanation teaches people to delete the explanation.

Classification: A the Swift repair · B the new regression suite · C the OTA
stamp · D/E/P/F: ZERO.

Not touched: the flight-recorder architecture, every measurement, the JS facade,
the event vocabulary, the derived semantics, llama configuration, the native-ML
scheduler, gameplay, artwork, build-ios.yml, the iOS build-number mechanic, the
promotion control plane, and every open punch-list item.

⚠ NO DEVICE VERIFICATION IS CLAIMED, and no archive success is claimed. The
recorder has still never run on hardware.
